units.text: Aspose.Email FOSS for Cpp reads and writes MSG and EML formats. It converts messages between MSG and EML representations. It creates new messages and saves them in MSG or EML format. It reads existing messages from streams or files and exposes their content.

It reads, builds, and writes generic Compound File Binary containers directly through cfb_reader, cfb_storage/cfb_stream, and cfb_writer, working with file paths, in-memory streams, or raw byte buffers.
It parses and reconstructs the raw MSG directory/stream structure with msg_reader, msg_document, and msg_writer, including an optional strict-validation mode surfaced through validation_issues().

It creates, edits, saves, and reloads Outlook-style messages through mapi_message, setting the subject, plain-text and HTML bodies, and sender identity, or reaching arbitrary MAPI properties via set_property()/get_property_value() with common_message_property_id and property_type_code.

It adds To/Cc/Bcc recipients with add_recipient(), attaches regular files from byte buffers or streams with add_attachment(), and nests a full mapi_message as an embedded-message attachment with add_embedded_message_attachment().
It saves an in-memory mapi_message to .eml and loads .eml back into a mapi_message, both through the library's own MIME engine, with no external MIME dependency.

Aspose.Email FOSS for Cpp provides the mapi_message class as the primary high-level entry point for creating, editing, and reloading messages, while lower-level classes such as msg_reader, msg_document, msg_writer, cfb_reader, cfb_document, and cfb_writer expose the underlying MSG and CFB container structure directly for callers that need it.
The aspose.email.foss namespace contains the public API surface for Aspose.Email FOSS for Cpp, including the mapi_message class for message authoring and the low-level MSG and CFB access classes.
The getting started guide covers installation, walkthroughs, and feature guides for this library.
The how-to guides and FAQ provide task-focused answers for common MSG, EML, and CFB processing questions.
The full API reference offers the complete, browsable reference for all 26 public types.
The public API surface documents the stable public namespaces and headers this library commits to.
The changelog records the release history.
Users can open an issue on GitHub to report bugs or request features.

Aspose.Email FOSS for Cpp reads and writes MSG, CFB, and EML containers and messages on disk, in memory, or in a stream; it is a file-format library for email message storage, not a mail client or transport library.

No SMTP, IMAP, POP3, or other network mail-protocol support — this library reads and writes MSG, CFB, and EML containers and messages already on disk, in memory, or in a stream; it is not a mail client or transport library.
No PST (Outlook Personal Folders) archive support — only single MSG-format messages and generic CFB containers are supported, not multi-message PST stores.

Only a curated subset of MAPI properties (subject, plain-text and HTML body, message class, sender name/address/address type, and Internet Message-ID) has a dedicated named accessor on mapi_message; every other property must be read and written through the generic get_property_value()/set_property() pair with common_message_property_id and property_type_code.

Aspose.Email FOSS for Cpp requires CMake 3.26 or later and a C++17 compiler, with the Ninja generator configured by the repository's default CMake preset. The project sets CMAKE_CXX_STANDARD to 17 and CMAKE_CXX_STANDARD_REQUIRED to ON, and no third-party dependencies are fetched during build or test. Test executables for the CFB layer, MSG layer, and public constants are registered with CTest and use only the standard library without an external test framework. Runnable examples reside in the examples/ directory and can be built separately by enabling ASPOSE_EMAIL_FOSS_BUILD_EXAMPLES while disabling ASPOSE_EMAIL_FOSS_BUILD_TESTS.
It adds mail-protocol connectivity, PST archive support, and broader MAPI property and format coverage across the full commercial product line.

The cfb_document class represents a Compound File Binary document and provides methods to load it from various sources and access its root storage, version information, and transaction signature number.
The cfb_exception class represents an error condition that occurs during Compound File Binary processing.
The cfb_node class represents a node in a Compound File Binary structure, providing access to its name, class identifier, timestamps, state bits, and whether it is a storage or stream.
The cfb_reader class reads a Compound File Binary document and provides access to its header, directory entries, FAT, mini FAT, DIFAT, and stream data.
The cfb_storage class represents a storage node in a Compound File Binary document and allows adding child storages and streams.
The cfb_stream class represents a stream node in a Compound File Binary document and provides access to its data.
The cfb_writer class writes a Compound File Binary document to a file or stream.
The directory_color_flag enumeration indicates the color of a directory entry in a Compound File Binary document.
The directory_entry class represents an entry in the directory of a Compound File Binary document and provides access to its name, class identifier, timestamps, color flag, and other metadata.
The directory_object_type enumeration specifies the type of object represented by a directory entry in a Compound File Binary document.
The header class represents the header of a Compound File Binary document and provides access to its metadata.
The sector_marker enumeration identifies special sector values in a Compound File Binary document.
The common_message_property_id enumeration defines standard property identifiers for MAPI messages.
The mapi_attachment class represents an attachment in a MAPI message.
The mapi_message class represents a MAPI message and provides methods to create, load, and save messages, as well as manage recipients, attachments, and properties.
The mapi_property class represents a single MAPI property.
The mapi_property_collection class represents a collection of MAPI properties.
The mapi_recipient class represents a recipient in a MAPI message.
The msg_document class represents a MSG document and provides access to its structure and content.
The msg_exception class represents an error condition that occurs during MSG processing.
The msg_reader class reads a MSG document and provides access to its internal structure.
The msg_storage class represents a storage node in a MSG document.
The msg_storage_role enumeration specifies the role of a storage node in a MSG document.
The msg_stream class represents a stream node in a MSG document.
The msg_writer class writes a MSG document to a file or stream.
The property_type_code enumeration defines MAPI property type codes.
